verdicts.reason: Every quote verified verbatim. 14.03.01-download-delivery-resumable-transfer.md:73 publishes a single per-artifact SHA-256 as copyable text; :82 shows it 'before any bytes move'; :89 auto-verifies it on completion; :114 (E-19) escalates a second mismatch as a bad stored artifact and quarantines the build; :184 (D-09) builds the air-gapped hand-verification workflow on that published value. The same delivery step is normatively specified to rewrite bytes per delivery: digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:455 and :464 (CX-24 q2) fix the order 'Grant issued -> embed tempo/key/loop metadata -> apply per-buyer watermark -> serve', 14.04.01-sample-loop-pack-catalog.md:275 (D-06) requires embedded tempo/key/loop metadata in delivered files, and 14.03.05-per-buyer-forensic-watermarking.md:39 stamps a buyer-unique mark during transfer. Band check kills the 'only a COULD feature' escape: moscow-ledger.md:136 (14.03.01) and :138 (14.04.01) are both in the MUST band (lines 17-216), so the metadata writer alone collides with the checksum at launch, watermarking aside. I searched every occurrence of sha-256/checksum/hash across all 62 files of domain 14 - the only hits are 14.03.01:73,74,82,89,100,104,114,119,132,180,184,193 and 14.09.03:52. Nothing anywhere reconciles a pre-published hash with delivery-time byte writes, and no [PENDING]/[OWNER]/[DEFERRED] marker covers it. The omission is conspicuous rather than accidental: 14.03.01 works out the watermark interaction in detail elsewhere - :85 and :105 (E-10) force a deterministic per-grant seed so resumed ranges regenerate byte-identically, :122 (E-27) handles stamping failure, DT-03/DT-07/DT-08 at :147,:151,:152 close out CDN, P2P and delta patching under marking - yet never touches the checksum. Two normative statements that cannot both hold, with no marker on either, and the failure is user-visible: under the spec as written every content download mismatches, trips E-19 twice and quarantines a correctly-delivered build while telling the buyer 'This file didn't verify. That's on us'. Blocking: the implementer cannot ship delivery without inventing an integrity contract (master hash vs post-stamp per-grant hash vs a second verification object), and D-09's hand-verification product promise changes under each choice.

The quote is near-verbatim (the auditor added bold around 'Flagged for confirmation.' which 14.03.05-per-buyer-forensic-watermarking.md:89 does not carry), and it is true that no Open Question at :95-:97 covers the failure posture. But the behaviour an implementer needs is fully and consistently stated in two places, one of them a MUST-band feature. 14.03.05:48 records the edge case as '~~Serve unmarked or fail the download?~~ **Resolved - this file's D-03**' and 14.03.05:63 gives the Error state ('download proceeds, incident logged; buyer sees nothing'). 14.03.01-download-delivery-resumable-transfer.md:122 (E-27) then restates it as binding delivery behaviour with no hedge at all - 'Per 14.03.05 D-03: serve unmarked, log the incident, never block a paying buyer... But the grant must record that this artifact is unmarked' - and 14.03.01 is MUST per moscow-ledger.md:136 while 14.03.05 is COULD per moscow-ledger.md:607. Two competent implementers both build fail-open-and-log; 'flagged for confirmation' is a note that the owner may later revisit a decision that is already made and already consumed downstream, not an unanswered question. No divergence, no forced invention.

The load-bearing cell is misquoted by ellipsis. 14.01.04-rig-profile-compatibility-checker.md:53 actually reads '| Buyer's declared rig is wrong (says macOS 14, actually on 12) | Verdict was confidently wrong; the good is non-returnable - the buyer is refunded regardless, cause `buyer-rig-error` | ~~`[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]`~~ **RESOLVED -> 14.09.02 D-02** (via Q-02 below)'. The marker is struck through and explicitly resolved; the finding's '...' hides that, and its forcedInvention ('the reader must decide whether the cell's outcome is 14.09.02 D-02's unconditional refund or something narrower') is answered by name in the very cell quoted. The claim 'One is an Edge Cases outcome cell, leaving a failure mode with no defined behaviour' is therefore false. The supporting evidence is also misquoted: 'digital-goods-marketplace-index.md:135-143, where every owner question is Deferral re-pointed from the completed /ideate-validate' - only Q-06 (:138) and Q-07 (:139) carry that phrase, it names /ideate-validate not /ideate-discover, and Q-03/Q-04/Q-05/Q-09/Q-10/Q-11 say no such thing. The three surviving cells are tracked by the ratified depth plan: 14.01-catalog-compatibility-cx.md:90 is the role-scoping line of CX-04, a 'Medium confidence' pair whose synthesis is deferred at :92, exactly the mechanism ideation-index.md:211 (D-25) ratifies ('5 questions answered for high-confidence pairs'); and 14.01.04 is COULD (moscow-ledger.md:603, COULD band 507-712), which ideation-index.md:210 (D-24) holds at [SURFACE] as 'correctly out of Step 5 scope'.

All five quotes exist verbatim, but every one sits in a unit the ratified depth plan deliberately leaves undeepened. moscow-ledger.md places 14.02.02 at :604 and 14.02.04 at :605 in the COULD band (507-712) and 14.02.03 at :750 in the WONT band (713-772); ideation-index.md:210 (D-24) locks that as intended state - 'Coulds (201) and Won'ts (53) correctly remain [SURFACE] - out of Step 5 scope'. An unfilled Edge Cases outcome on a [SURFACE] COULD/WONT feature is the documented output of the plan, not a gap in it, and none of these features is in the launch set, so no implementer is forced to invent anything to build v1. The chargeback-fraud cell (14.02.04-serial-blacklisting-anti-piracy.md:52) additionally sits in a feature whose own DT-01 the domain records as near-useless on this catalog (cited at digital-goods-marketplace-index.md and 14.03.05:12-13). The fifth cell, 14.02-licensing-activation-entitlement-cx.md:109, is the role-scoping line of CX-05, a 'Medium confidence' pair (:104) whose synthesis at :111 is explicitly 'Deferred - Medium confidence; contingent on reseller integration being obtainable at all (14.02.03 Q-01)' - a named contingency pointing at a tracked question, and precisely the medium-confidence carve-out ratified at ideation-index.md:211 (D-25).

All quotes verified verbatim, but the contradiction does not survive the surrounding normative text. 14.09.01-withdrawal-right-waiver-capture.md:216 (D-08) is the governing rule: 'The gate does not branch on territory; it fires for every buyer, and only the wording varies by locale... Neutral wording outside the EU/UK/EEA'. E-20 (:144) is that locale variant, and E-01 (:125) is the EU/UK variant of the same message - the mechanism for selecting between them is stated, so an implementer does not choose between 'the promise' and 'the silence'; they render the locale variant D-08 mandates. The finding also misreads which element E-01 requires to be stated: the sentence lists three options and 'The third option is stated' refers to the day-15 self-disable ('or wait: from <date> this download will start without asking'), confirmed by D-09 at :217 - 'the decline message states the date the gate stops asking'. Neutral wording therefore still has a stated exit, and the claimed contradiction with D-09 evaporates. What genuinely remains open - whether a US buyer with no statutory floor is offered a discretionary pre-download cancellation - is tracked with both an owner and a target, on exactly this reasoning: 14.09.01:229 (Q-01) '`[OWNER]` ... what is the refund policy above the statutory floor ... Sharpened by Q-04's resolution: with a US-first launch there is no statutory floor to sit above, so the policy is not a top-up - it is the entire consumer position. | User | `/create-prd`', mirrored at 14.09.02:293 (Q-01). Finally, the sibling is not 'restated as unconditional behaviour': 14.09.02:149-:150 and :279 (D-06) cite 2011/83/EU Art. 9(2)(a) by name, and :164 scopes the duty explicitly - 'refusal is unlawful in the EU/UK'.
